Subject: SomniHealth evaluation plan — initial recap and proposed scope

Emma — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Goal: Validate a production-grade Q&A assistant on SomniHealth patient support workflows (billing & intake) with a focus on accuracy and hallucination reduction.
- Data: you mentioned ~25k anonymized transcripts and an internal KB (~1200 docs). Confirmed PHI will be removed prior to transfer; you'll send a redacted sample.
- Success metrics: >= 86% top-1 correctness on our benchmark questions; <2% high-confidence hallucinations in the accepted prompts.

Recommended Redwood approach (high level):
1) Short pilot eval (2 weeks): run parallel model candidates across the same prompt bank and scoring rubric.
2) Scoring: mixed automatic (exact/EM, BLEU where applicable) + human adjudication for intent/accuracy and hallucination flags.
3) Logistics: you provide a 200–500 sample CSV (rows: id, context, question, expected_answer) and we run the first pass on Redwood hosted infra.

Attached is a lightweight template we use for bench samples (redwood_eval_template_v1.xlsx). Ben (cc) will follow up with model recommendations and scoring detail.

Next steps: can you share the redacted sample by EOD Thursday 8/20? If so, we can lock in a kickoff for Monday 8/24 and deliver the initial candidate comparison by 9/4.

Thanks — Karthik

Subject: Re: SomniHealth evaluation plan — model candidates, dataset format & scoring

Hi Emma — quick technical note and answers to the two asks. TL;DR: we recommend comparing two quantized open candidates + our Redwood-curated L2 baseline; dataset format below.

Model recommendations (candidate set):
- M1: open-llm-13b-qat (8-bit quant) — low latency, good on instruction-following for Q&A.
- M2: llama-2-13b-instruct-q8 — slightly higher quality on multi-turn context; we expect fewer context drop errors.
- Baseline: redwood-l2-chat-small — curated and tuned by Redwood with safety filters; useful for regression detection.

How we measure hallucination / "high-confidence hallucination":
- We compute a hallucination score by combining token-level logprob thresholds with a factuality classifier. High-confidence hallucination = classifier_probability >= 0.85 AND average token-logprob below -1.6. 
- We report counts and examples; human adjudicators validate a 10% sample to calibrate thresholds.

Dataset format (required CSV columns):
- id (string), context (string, optional), question (string), expected_answer (string), answer_type (enum: span/freeform/multi), priority (low/med/high)
- KB docs: single-zip of PDFs/TXT; we accept a sitemap.csv linking doc_id to filename. For the initial pilot the KB can be a small subset (100 docs).

Scoring rubric (we'll run automatic + human):
- Automatic: exact match (span), normalized EM for short answers, semantic-similarity score (embedding cosine) for freeform with threshold 0.82.
- Human: labeler checks accuracy, partial credit, hallucination_flag (yes/no), severity (low/medium/high). Final score = weighted sum (auto 60% / human 40%).

Attachments: I uploaded a sample dataset template and a short runbook to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSomniEval (folder contains redwood_eval_template_v1.xlsx and somni_eval_dataset_sample.csv).

Security/compliance note: for the pilot we'll run on Redwood hosted with strict access controls and per-project keys; for production we can move to Dedicated or Private deployment with an attestation and contract addendum. Marissa (cc) can drive the compliance checklist.

If that sounds good I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff to align the ingestion workflow and labeler criteria.

— Ben
